title.narrative: Plan International Sverige Digital Skills 4 Youth 2023-2026
Plan International Sweden Digital Skills 4 Youth 2023-2026

description.narrative: Ansökan om finansieringsstöd från Plan International Sverige för ett projekt med titeln ”Digital Skills 4 Youth Project 2023-2026”, syftar till att utforma ett program för ungdomars anställbarhet och entreprenörskap underbyggt av digitala färdigheter med olika tvärsektoriella och urban-landsbygdskopplingar.

The application for funding support by Plan International Sweden for a project titled Digital Skills 4 Youth Project 2023-2026, seeks to model a youth employability and entrepreneurship programme underpinned by digital skills with various cross-sectoral and urban-rural linkages.

The broad outcome of the proposal is to enhance sustainable, productive economic development for youth, particularly young women in a supportive environment for digital skills entrepreneurship and employment in targeted areas. The intervention has identified outcomes as key in achieving the set objective:
Outcome 1
1,680 young people, including young women in the targeted areas have strengthened skills relevant for the digital labour market. An additional 3000 young people will be reached under the virtual market intervention.
Outcome 2
Targeted areas have strengthened structures for young people's professional development including linkages with the digital labour market, especially for young women
Outcome 3
Private and governmental sectors on a national and local level have taken actions to enhance young women's economic rights and economic participation
Young women in Zimbabwe face high rates of unemployment coupled with its negative effects including lack of livelihood, and high rates of negative coping mechanisms (e.g. crime, drug abuse and risky health behaviors). There is a huge digital divide in Zimbabwe that cannot be ignored if digital skills programmes are to be truly equitable. The proposal recognizes that globally, evidence points to the relevance of digital skills in the trending job market, with the digital economy contributing 15.5% to the global Gross Domestic Product (GDP), a percentage expected to increase to 25% by year 2025. The intervention is expected to impact young peoples digital skills, enabling their sustainable income-generation through either entrepreneurship or employment.
The project offers two streams of digital skills interventions; that is, tailored for rural and urban youth particularly young women. It is envisaged that the basic digital skills stream coupled with the MakerSpace model will enable rural youth to perform ICT-enhanced trades through entrepreneurship or employment; whilst the intermediate/advanced digital skills stream coupled with the job market linkages will enhance urban youths employability or entrepreneurship in the digital economy. MakerSpace is Impact Hubs model hinged on physical hubs equipped to provide technical training on agro-processing that incorporates imparting basic digital skills needed to enhance the chosen trades.
The embassy assesses the objectives of the intervention and the expected results to be achievable.

As this is a new agreement, there will be no results.
The results will be published at the end of 2024 after implementation.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
